summary: This paper initiates the study of spectral Sidon sets in matrix algebras over integer boxes and finite fields. The author establishes universal commuting ceilings via Wedderburn-Minkowski packing, determines the exact asymptotic exponent for non-commuting integer matrices using hierarchical Hessenberg spectral decoding, explores the arithmetic rift between symmetric and non-symmetric matrices via Landau-Ramanujan theory, and investigates finite-field spectral Sidon sets and Galois torus hierarchies. All core results are machine-checked in Lean 4.
strengths: Pioneers a natural and profound non-abelian generalisation of classical Sidon sets.
Provides tight matching asymptotic bounds across commutative and non-commutative matrix spaces.
Combines sophisticated algebraic number theory, analytic number theory, and formal verification in Lean 4 (0 sorry).
weaknesses: Some bounds in the symmetric and hyperbolic cases leave logarithmic gaps that motivate interesting open conjectures.
The combinatorial machinery involves complex hierarchical expansions that require careful verification.
strong_novelty_candidates: Initiation of Spectral Sidon Sets in matrix algebras with exact asymptotic exponent Theta_d(N^{d(d+1)/4}) via Hierarchical Hessenberg Spectral Decoding.
Landau-Ramanujan symmetric-vs-non-symmetric arithmetic rift in Sym_2([0,N]) and super-exponential Galois-torus separation over F_p.
